values.summary: Run ten 7.5-hour/64,000-token episode waves plus a separately scheduled 5-hour/60,000-token integration wave inside the fixed 80-agent-hour/700,000-token aggregate; five parallel owners produce complete reviewed packages and stop before deployment or publication.

steps.action: Verify #5819, #3223/#3256, route/storage authority, and budget 10 x 1.75-hour/21,000-token source-and-script waves
Budget 10 x 2.25-hour/16,000-token production waves for generation, editing, and mastered audio
Budget 10 x 1.5-hour/13,000-token packaging waves for transcripts, notes, artwork, metadata, manifests, and RSS enclosures
Budget 10 x 1.5-hour/10,000-token listen-review and revision waves, including consent and redaction review
Budget 10 x 30-minute/4,000-token machine-validation waves and implement the three owned playback producers
Use the allocated 5-hour/60,000-token integration wave for feed consistency, digest-recomputed platform playback, exact-head review, and final revisions
Define and verify podcast rollback: restore feed/readiness records, remove only issue-owned packages and producers, retain QA evidence, and perform no deployment or publication action.

invariants: Every final audio digest matches its manifest and enclosure
Guest state never exceeds consent evidence
Feed records contain stable public-safe values, not local paths
Temporary validation state remains inside issue evidence
risks: Audio generation or mastering may vary by provider/platform
Guest and artwork rights may block individual episodes
Large binary artifacts may exceed repository policy
stop_conditions: Route/storage or binary-artifact policy is unresolved
Required consent or source rights are unavailable
Audio QA cannot produce deterministic manifests
A credential would need to enter tracked evidence
Rollback would delete upstream production proof, mutate consent, or require feed deployment/publication.
replan_triggers: Episode briefs or guest states change
Feed, audio, artwork, or repository-size policy changes
